All paths are under <repo>/src.

**1. src/session-paths.js**
- It does not enumerate session files. Its only export is `recentToolPaths(transcriptPath, { root, limit = 15, tailBytes = TAIL_BYTES } = {})` (session-paths.js:83).
- Claude Code session enumeration lives in src/parser.js:
  - `discoverSessionFiles(options = {})` (parser.js:329). Options are `{ projectFilter, days = 30, excludeSessionPath, root = CLAUDE_DIR, now }`. It returns `[{ path, projectDir, mtime, size, subagentFiles? }]` sorted by mtime ascending (parser.js:367, 383).
  - `listSubagentFiles(sessionDir, projectDir, cutoff)` (parser.js:391).
  - `dedupeSessionFiles(files)` (parser.js:420).
- Codex rollout handling is in src/codex/ledger.js, not in session-paths.js. I only saw its export list, and I did not find a Codex rollout file enumerator there.
  - `loadCodexLedger`, `readCodexDelegations` and `readCodexBindings` are exports there.
  - Line 210 has a comment about "the route id a child rollout carries".
  - Other files mentioning "rollout" are handoff.js, team-sync.js, installer.js, team-prompts.js, and codex/hooks.js, panel-shell.js, harness.js and doctor.js.

**2. src/route-scan.js (per-turn user prompt "episodes")**
- The function is `toEpisodes(records)` (route-scan.js:282). It is not exported.
- It groups consecutive records that share the same `userText` into one episode. Each episode has these fields (route-scan.js:286-293):
  - `text` (the trimmed `r.userText`)
  - `calls`, `out`, `mutating`, `errors`, `delegated`
  - `models` (a Set)
  - `cwd`, `tools`
  - `delegationToolUseIds`
  - `startedAt` and `endedAt` (epoch ms, from `r.timestamp`)
- Episodes have no `label`, `ts` or `file` field.
  - The caller at route-scan.js:612-614 pushes `{ ep, projectDir: f.projectDir, sessionPath: f.path }` into `all`, skipping episodes with empty `text`.
  - The `label: cat.label` fields at route-scan.js:693 and 866 are category labels, not episode labels.
- Related exports: `isSkippable(text)` (route-scan.js:276) and `episodeRank(ep)`.

**3. Records, parser, transcript lines**
- src/session-records.js:
  - `normalizeModelId`.
  - `collectSessionRecords(filePath, { includeContent = true } = {})` (session-records.js:90). It is async and returns an array of per-request records, one per assistant request id, not per JSONL line.
  - `CARRY_CAP` and `COMPACTION_RATIO` (consts).
  - `delegationContexts(records)` (session-records.js:235).
- `collectSessionRecords` record fields:
  - `timestamp`: `entry.timestamp || null` (session-records.js:180).
  - Token counts: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `ephemeral5m`, `ephemeral1h`.
  - `depth`.
  - `userText`: the last user text seen, empty if `includeContent` is false.
  - `assistantText`.
  - `cwd`.
  - Counts and ids: `mutatingToolCalls`, `delegationCalls`, `delegationToolUseIds`, `toolErrors`, `toolCounts`, `textChars`, `delegationResults`.
  - `model`, via `normalizeModelId`.
- There is no `role` field. The user role is read from `entry.type === 'user'` (session-records.js:106-110).
- It has no byte-offset parameter. It reads the whole file through `transcriptLines`.
- src/transcript-lines.js: the sole export is `async function* transcriptLines(filePath)` (transcript-lines.js:31). It yields raw lines, handles `.zst` files, and has no offset support (it uses a plain `createReadStream`).
- src/parser.js exports:
  - `parseSessionFile(filePath)`
  - `getSessionModel`
  - `getLastUserMessageTime`
  - `discoverSessionFiles`
  - `listSubagentFiles`
  - `dedupeSessionFiles`
  - `parseAllSessions`
  - `sessionsSince`
- The only byte-position reading I saw in parser.js is tail scanning: `scanTail`, `lastUserTsFromTail` and `getLastUserMessageTime`. I read `scanTail` only as far as its return shapes, not its signature. Treat it as tail-only rather than an arbitrary offset reader.

**4. Spend per calendar day**
- `dailyTrend(sessions)` in stats.js:30 returns per-day token and cache stats. Its fields are date, input, cacheCreation, cacheRead, ephemeral5m, ephemeral1h, output, apiCalls, sessions, hitRate and totalInput. It has no cost field.
- Per-UTC-day token totals by model:
  - `parseSessionFile` output carries `dayTotals`, shaped `{ 'YYYY-MM-DD': { model: totals } }`. It is built in parser.js `sumRequests`, with the return at parser.js:204 and the spread at parser.js:121.
  - claude-price.js:49-53 iterates `dayTotals`.
  - `usageSince(sinceMs, { exclude = new Set() } = {})` (usage-ledger.js:95) returns parts of the form `{ id, model, totals, at, byDay, own }`. It keeps per-day tokens, and its header says it never stores dollars.
- The only function I found that returns a dollar figure per day is `aggregateDaily({ now, dir, days = 30, sessions, coworkSessions, codexSessions, codexLedger, codexDocEvents, codexPrices, gatewayDaily, env })` in team-sync.js:395.
  - Its per-day map holds `spent, subagent, codex, saved, runs, cost, codexRuns, codexCost, unpriced, fam, models`.
  - I did not read its return value.
- `fetchGatewayDailySpend(...)` (gateway-spend.js:135) and `gatewayDayValue(result, day)` (gateway-spend.js:122) cover gateway daily spend.
- cost.js exports `estimateCost(totals, model, { price, at })` (cost.js:404) and `estimateCostAcross(sessions, estimate)` (cost.js:569), neither of which is per day.
- I did not open any month-spend function.

It walks `<root>/<projectDir>/*.jsonl` and keeps files with mtime >= cutoff. It returns `{ path, projectDir, mtime, size, subagentFiles? }[]`, deduped and sorted by mtime ascending.
  - `listSubagentFiles(sessionDir, projectDir, cutoff)` at parser.js:391 reads `<session>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl` and returns `{ path, projectDir, mtime, size }[]`.
  - `dedupeSessionFiles(files)` at parser.js:420 keeps one file per basename, preferring the larger one, then the newer.
- The Codex rollout enumerator is `discoverCodexSessionFiles({ home = codexUserDir(), days = 30, excludeSessionPath, compressed = false } = {})` at src/codex/parser.js:470. It recursively walks `<home>/sessions` and `<home>/archived_sessions` for `.jsonl` files, plus `.jsonl.zst` only when `compressed` is true. It returns `{ path, mtime, size }[]` sorted by mtime.

**2. route-scan.js prompt extraction**
- The function is `toEpisodes(records)` at route-scan.js:282. It is not exported.
- It does not read JSONL itself. It consumes `collectSessionRecords(f.path, { includeContent: true })` (called at :608) and groups consecutive records that share the same `r.userText.trim()`.
- Each returned episode has these fields: `text, calls, out, mutating, errors, delegated, models (Set), cwd, tools ({name: n}), delegationToolUseIds [], startedAt, endedAt`. `startedAt` and `endedAt` are the min and max of `Date.parse(r.timestamp)` in ms (:286-319).
- Episodes carry no `label`, `ts` or `file` field. In `runRouteScan` (:586) the caller wraps each one as `{ ep, projectDir: f.projectDir, sessionPath: f.path }` (:612-614) and skips episodes with empty `ep.text`.
- `label` and `labelEn` are set later from the category or group (`label: cat.label` at :693, `label: g.label` at :866). They are not per-prompt fields.

**3. Parser, record and line readers**
- `src/transcript-lines.js` exports only `async function* transcriptLines(filePath)` (:31). It yields raw line strings from the start of the file through readline over `createReadStream`, and it decompresses `.zst` on the fly. It has no offset parameter.
- `src/session-records.js` exports:
  - `normalizeModelId(model)` at :18
  - `collectSessionRecords(filePath, { includeContent = true } = {})` at :90
  - `CARRY_CAP = 50` at :217
  - `COMPACTION_RATIO = 0.5` at :219
  - `delegationContexts(records)` at :235
- `collectSessionRecords` iterates `transcriptLines` and returns one record per assistant API request (keyed by requestId). It does not return one record per user message.
  - A user entry only updates `lastUserText`. That value is copied into each assistant record as `userText` (:108-111, :198).
  - Record fields: `model, timestamp, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, input_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, cache_read_tokens, ephemeral5m, ephemeral1h, depth, userText, assistantText, cwd, mutatingToolCalls, delegationCalls, delegationToolUseIds, toolErrors, toolCounts, textChars, delegationResults`.
  - It has no role field and no byte-offset support.
- `src/parser.js` exports:
  - `parseSessionFile(filePath)` at :29
  - `getSessionModel(filePath)` at :291
  - `getLastUserMessageTime(filePath)` at :301
  - `discoverSessionFiles` at :329
  - `listSubagentFiles` at :391
  - `dedupeSessionFiles` at :420
  - `parseAllSessions(options = {})` at :488
  - `sessionsSince(sessions, sinceMs, { noCache = false } = {})` at :612
  - It has no offset parameter on any export. The internal `scanTail(filePath, hint, visit)` at :231 reads only the tail.
- Byte-related readers elsewhere:

  - A comment at codex/parser.js:474 says "src/team-prompts.js reads rollouts by byte offset". That file exports `codexPromptFromLine(line)` at team-prompts.js:186. I did not inspect its offset reader.

That grep was cut at 10 lines; only 5 matched, so the list is complete. I did not open any of them except `transcript-lines.js`, so I did not find a Codex rollout enumeration function.
- `transcript-lines.js` mentions Codex `.zst` rollouts in its header comment and handles `.zst` paths.

**2. `src/route-scan.js` episodes**
- The extraction function is `toEpisodes(records)` at `route-scan.js:282`. It is not exported. It takes records from `collectSessionRecords`.
- It groups consecutive records that share the same `userText`, trimmed, into one episode.
- Each episode object has these fields: `text`, `calls`, `out`, `mutating`, `errors`, `delegated`, `models` (a Set), `cwd`, `tools` (a name-to-count map), `delegationToolUseIds`, `startedAt` and `endedAt`.
- `startedAt` and `endedAt` are epoch milliseconds, the min and max of `Date.parse(r.timestamp)`.
- There is no `label`, `ts` or `file` field on these objects. The `label` hits at `route-scan.js:693` and `:866` are `cat.label` and `g.label`, which are category and group labels.
- I did not read where `toEpisodes` is called, so I don't know whether the source file is attached elsewhere.
- Related exports I saw:
  - `categorize(text, toolCounts)` and `categorizeScored(text, toolCounts)` (returns `{cat, score}`).
  - `isSkippable(text)`, using `SKIP_RE` and `SKIP_PREFIX`.
  - `episodeRank(ep)`.
  - `dominantModel(counts)`.
  - `isFailedRun(run)`.
  - `mungeProjectPath(p)`.
  - `routeScanCachePath()`.

**3. Raw JSONL records**
- `src/transcript-lines.js` exports one function, `transcriptLines(filePath)` at `transcript-lines.js:31`. It is an async generator that yields raw line strings. It handles `.zst`.
- `src/session-records.js` exports:
  - `normalizeModelId(model)` at `:18`.
  - `collectSessionRecords(filePath, { includeContent = true } = {})` at `:90`.
  - `CARRY_CAP` at `:217` and `COMPACTION_RATIO` at `:219`.
  - `delegationContexts(records)` at `:235`.
- `collectSessionRecords` is the one that yields per-API-call records, not per-turn user records. It is async and returns `[...records.values()]`.
- Each record has `model`, `timestamp` (the entry's timestamp), `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `input_tokens`, `cache_creation_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `ephemeral5m`, `ephemeral1h`, `depth`, `userText`, `assistantText`, `cwd`, `mutatingToolCalls`, `delegationCalls`, `delegationToolUseIds`, `toolErrors`, `toolCounts`, `textChars` and `delegationResults`.
- It has no `role` field. `userText` is the most recent user message text (`session-records.js:~152`), and `assistantText` and `userText` are empty when `includeContent` is false.
- Records are keyed by `entry.requestId || msg.id`. Entries with `<synthetic>` models, or without `msg.usage` or `msg.id`, are skipped.
- Byte offset: none of `transcriptLines(filePath)`, `collectSessionRecords(filePath, opts)` or `parseSessionFile(filePath)` (`parser.js:29`) takes an offset. A grep for `offset|start:|position` in `parser.js`, `session-records.js` and `transcript-lines.js` found none. The only `createReadStream` is in `transcript-lines.js`, called without `start`.
- `parser.js` also has tail-based readers (`getSessionModel` at `:291`, `getLastUserMessageTime` at `:301`). I did not read `scanTail` or `lastUserTsFromTail`.
- Other `parser.js` exports: `sessionsSince(sessions, sinceMs, { noCache = false } = {})` at `:612`.

**4. Daily cost**
- `dailyTrend(sessions)` at `stats.js:30` is the only per-day function I saw.
- It returns an array sorted by `date`. Each element has `date`, `input`, `cacheCreation`, `cacheRead`, `ephemeral5m`, `ephemeral1h`, `output`, `apiCalls`, `sessions`, `hitRate` and `totalInput`, plus whatever `addLong` adds.
- It has no cost field. It buckets by `dateKey(s.startTime)`, i.e. the session start day, not the per-request timestamp.
- Other `stats.js` exports: `ttlBreakdown`, `detectAnomalies`, `sessionMetrics`, `computeBaseline`, `diagnoseSession`, `detectSpikes`, `detectContextWindow`, `summary`.
- I did not search the pricing or cost modules. I can't say whether a per-day dollar function exists elsewhere in the code.
